native_region: Central America, Caribbean, and northern South America
habitat: Widely cultivated in gardens, temples, and institutional campuses
ecological_importance: Night-fragrant flowers attract hawkmoths and specialized nocturnal insect pollinators. All parts of the plant contain toxic latex deterring mammalian herbivores.
threats: None significant due to extensive horticultural propagation.
conservation_actions: Maintained as ornamental landscape flora on institutional campuses.
field_identification_notes: Thick, succulent, club-like grey branches exuding white latex when broken.
Crowded, elongated lanceolate leaves clustered tightly at branch tips.
Large, strongly fragrant white flowers with yellow centers.
ml_relevance: Thick succulent branch architecture, clustered terminal lanceolate leaves, and white-yellow flowers.

ar_information.quick_identification: Thick succulent branches; leaves clustered at tips; fragrant white flowers with yellow centers.
ar_information.conservation_message: Least Concern / Widely Cultivated. Despite its delicate appearance, the branches are filled with caustic white latex that protects the tree from herbivores.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Campus garden beds and entrance courtyards
